entries.title: Slow Motion
entries.text:
Slow Motion

OvercrankingRalenti

Slow motion cinematography plays action over more screen time than the event occupied during capture, usually by overcranking (recording 120 to 240 fps and playing at 24). The extra samples reveal fabric delay, particle hang, and impact mechanics that a 24 fps shutter would compress into a few smeared frames.

Volume

Create this Slow Motion

Narrative function

Use it when a second already contains a scene: a fall, a look that decides, a hit whose mechanics matter. Stretching the instant can turn it into dread, grief, or inspection.

Sound is half the meaning. Stretched diegetic noise makes the world heavy.

Real-time audio against slow picture can feel like a memory or a lie. It is the wrong tool when the beat needs speed, comic timing, or spatial inspection of a frozen pose.

If the camera orbits a nearly stopped body, you wanted bullet time. If frames are duplicated and smeared, you wanted step printing.

Do not slow every punch or the rate stops meaning anything.

How it works

Capture at a higher frame rate than playback and keep a planned shutter (often 180 degrees, so 120 fps is about 1/240 s per frame). You need more light because each exposure is shorter.

Keep gravity, contacts, and anatomy continuous through the extra samples. For generated footage, ask for real intermediate motion, not interpolated mush.

Prompt: Slow motion of [Subject] at 120 to 240 fps playback, dust hanging, fabric delayed, continuous gravity.

When to use it

Use it on a decisive instant a normal rate would hide, such as a glass leaving a waiter's hand. Do not use it as a default look for an entire fight.

Compared with similar shots

Constant slow motion is not a Speed Ramp, which changes rate inside the shot and then recovers. It is not Step Printing, which duplicates low-rate, long-exposure frames into a stuttered lyric smear.

It is not Bullet Time, which decouples a traveling viewpoint from near-frozen action. Freeze Frame stops sampling altogether.

Fast Motion and Time-Lapse crush duration instead of stretching it.

Speed RampMark one instant inside a fight or a look.

Step PrintingLonging that cannot move at normal speed.

Fast MotionToo much life for real time.

In film

Seven Samurai stretches the kidnapper's fall so the death occupies more than its wall-clock instant. The Wild Bunch fragments gunfights through varied slow-motion views so violence becomes duration.

The Matrix is often filed here, but the rooftop lean is closer to bullet time. In the Mood for Love belongs with step printing more than with clean overcranked silk.

Seven Samurai 1954The rescued child’s kidnapper falls in slowed motion.

The Wild Bunch 1969Violence is fragmented and expanded through varied slow-motion views.

Prompt it

Name the fps feel and what the extra time reveals. Still: a physically plausible mid-action pose with hanging dust, delayed fabric, and readable contacts, not a statue.

Video: Slow-motion 6-second shot of [Subject], time stretched, particles hanging in light, 120fps feel, locked or simple camera, no frozen background orbit.

Use in Video Generator

A glass slips from a waiter’s hand and falls in elegant slow motion. Fingers release naturally, the glass rotates coherently and fabric moves with plausible inertia. Locked close shot, smooth temporal detail, no frozen background or bullet-time orbit.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Bullet Time or a freeze. The tell is a stopped body with a moving camera, or a still with no new frames of motion.

Fix: keep the subject traveling through the action, keep anatomy and gravity continuous, and specify 120 to 240 fps playback rather than an orbit around a sculpture.

Questions

What is Slow Motion in film?

Slow motion is overcranked or retimed footage that occupies more screen time than the event took to happen, so small physical details become readable.

Slow Motion vs Bullet Time

Slow motion stretches the subject's action while the camera may stay simple. Bullet time nearly freezes the action while the viewpoint travels around it.

When should I use Slow Motion?

When one second already contains the scene: a fall, a look, or an impact whose mechanics or grief need extra duration.

How do I prompt Slow Motion for AI image or video?

Write 120 to 240 fps playback, delayed fabric, hanging particles, and continuous anatomy. Forbid a frozen subject with an orbiting camera.

entries.title: Fast Motion
entries.text:
Fast Motion

undercranking

Fast motion cinematography compresses screen duration so action plays faster than it occurred, by undercranking the camera or by retiming a normal-rate take. Crowds smear, clouds race, and labor can look absurdly efficient because too many events occupy too little time.

Volume

Create this Fast Motion

Narrative function

Use it when real time cannot hold the life in front of the lens: a factory that never stops, a city that should feel over-efficient, a chase whose danger is relentlessness rather than one punch. Subtle acceleration can be funnier or more oppressive than a cartoon speed-up.

Keep sound on its own clock. Pitch-shifted footsteps often betray the trick.

It is the wrong tool for weather, construction, or a night becoming morning. Those need interval sampling, not sped-up continuous action.

If the camera itself steps through space while hours collapse, you wanted a hyperlapse. Do not accelerate a performance whose contacts and gravity must stay honest.

How it works

Undercrank (shoot fewer frames per second than playback) or retime in the cut with a planned speed ratio. Longer exposure per frame, if the shutter stays open, increases motion blur.

Check hands, object contacts, and foot cadence after the speed change. Prompt: Undercranked fast motion of [Subject], crowds smearing, clouds racing, planned speed ratio, coherent contacts.

When to use it

Use it when a mailroom, assembly line, or crowd must feel over-efficient, as in a comic or cosmic crush of ordinary work. Do not use it to stand in for a day-to-night sky.

Compared with similar shots

Fast motion speeds continuous action. Time-Lapse samples the world at long intervals so slow change (shadows, crowds as systems) plays quickly.

Hyperlapse is time-lapse plus a camera that advances through space. Slow Motion is the inverse stretch.

A Speed Ramp changes rate inside one shot rather than holding a constant acceleration.

Time-LapseShow weather, construction, or a night becoming morning.

HyperlapseShow duration as velocity.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

In film

Modern Times uses factory rhythm so mechanized work feels like a speeded machine wearing a man. A Clockwork Orange undercranks selected passages so appetite and violence become brisk, grotesque efficiency.

Mad Max: Fury Road alters cadence on chosen action beats rather than running the whole film as a cartoon. Koyaanisqatsi is often grouped here, but its urban crush is mostly interval time-lapse.

Modern Times 1936Factory rhythms exaggerate the pressure of mechanized work.

Mad Max: Fury Road 2015Selected action beats use altered motion cadence and speed.

Prompt it

State that time is compressed and what races. Still: a pose that implies acceleration (smeared extras, streaked traffic) while the subject, if they must stay readable, holds.

Video: Fast-motion view of [Subject] and the environment, time compressed, crowds and weather racing, coherent hands and footsteps, not a motionless sun over a smoking crowd.

Use in Video Generator

A harried mailroom worker sorts envelopes in slightly accelerated motion while maintaining physically coherent hand actions. Fixed medium-wide view, increasingly comic efficiency, no teleporting objects or time-lapse crowd trails. Retime a clean base shot if exact cadence is required.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Time-Lapse. The tell is a racing crowd under a sun and shadows that never move, or people who teleport instead of stepping.

Fix: keep continuous action and a planned speed ratio, then check contacts. If hours must collapse, change to interval photography.

Questions

What is Fast Motion in film?

Fast motion is undercranked or retimed action that occupies less screen time than it took in the world, so movement looks accelerated.

Fast Motion vs Time-Lapse

Fast motion speeds a continuous take. Time-lapse captures frames at long intervals so processes too slow for real time (light, weather, crowds as flow) play in seconds.

When should I use Fast Motion?

When ordinary movement should feel over-efficient, comic, or relentless, and the action itself is still a continuous performance.

How do I prompt Fast Motion for AI image or video?

Write undercranked or accelerated playback, crowds and weather racing, and coherent contacts. Do not ask for hours of sun travel unless you actually want time-lapse.

entries.title: Speed Ramp
entries.text:
Speed Ramp

Variable-speed actionRalenti accéléré

Speed ramping changes playback or capture speed inside a single shot rather than holding one retiming ratio. Approach and recovery stay energetic while one motivated instant (impact, glance, turn) stretches, then the clock returns.

Volume

Create this Speed Ramp

Narrative function

Treat it as temporal close-up. The shot walks up in real time, lands on the fact that matters, and releases.

A fight, a catch, a look across a room can all take the ramp if the event is readable. The audience should feel one continuous action, not a new clip glued on.

It is the wrong tool when the whole beat should stay slow, or when you only need a smash of magnification. If rate never returns, you shot slow motion and called it a ramp.

If the picture punches in by focal length, you wanted a crash zoom. Do not ramp to hide unreadable choreography.

How it works

Capture enough temporal detail (high frame rate) that both the fast and slow portions have samples. Identify the motivated event, then shape the acceleration curve and matching motion blur.

The body must stay mechanically continuous through the change. Prompt: Speed ramp on [Subject], real time slamming into slow motion at the impact or glance, then releasing.

When to use it

Use it to mark one instant inside a fight or a look, such as a board leaving the ramp at the peak of a jump. Do not use it on every cut or the emphasis dies.

Compared with similar shots

A ramp is not constant Slow Motion, which never returns to real time. It is not a Crash Zoom In, which changes focal length rather than the clock.

Freeze Frame holds one image. Bullet Time lets the camera orbit a nearly stopped instant instead of stretching and releasing the same viewpoint's action.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

Crash Zoom InPunctuate a hit, a realization, or a comic sting.

Fast MotionToo much life for real time.

In film

300 moves combat between fast and extended slow-motion beats so selected blows become readable. Sherlock Holmes (2009) isolates anticipated fight details, then snaps back to the hit as performed.

The Matrix mixes rates around chosen impacts, though its array orbits are a different machine.

300 2006Combat moves between fast and extended slow-motion beats.

Sherlock Holmes 2009Anticipated combat details are isolated before action resumes.

Prompt it

Name the real-time approach, the stretched beat, and the recovery. Still: three readable phases implied in one pose is weaker than a video ramp.

Video: Speed ramp: real-time movement of [Subject] suddenly stretches into slow motion at the key beat, then recovers. One coherent action, readable contacts, natural gravity.

Use in Video Generator

A skateboarder approaches a small ramp at normal speed, slows smoothly to reveal the board rotating beneath their feet, then returns to normal speed on landing. One coherent action, readable foot placement, natural gravity, no impossible extra spin. Specify and refine the ramp in editing.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is wall-to-wall Slow Motion. The tell is a shot that never returns to real time, or a jump in pose at the speed change.

Fix: write approach, hold, and release, and keep the body continuous through the curve.

Questions

What is Speed Ramp in film?

A speed ramp is a change of playback or capture speed inside one shot, used to emphasize a single instant and then return.

Speed Ramp vs Slow Motion

Slow motion holds one stretched rate. A speed ramp enters that rate at a motivated event and leaves it, so approach and recovery stay fast.

When should I use Speed Ramp?

When one contact, recognition, or turn must be inspected without draining the energy of the surrounding action.

How do I prompt Speed Ramp for AI image or video?

Write real time into slow motion at a named beat, then recovery. Demand one continuous action and matching motion blur, not a cut to a different clip.

entries.title: Freeze Frame
entries.text:
Freeze Frame

Pre-existing song placementFeatured song cue

A freeze frame holds one image so narrative time stops while camera, subject, and world all cease to generate new samples. The hold can end a story, land a joke, or present a face as evidence.

Volume

Create this Freeze Frame

Narrative function

Use it when the fact is the picture itself: a boy at the edge of the sea, a narrator labeling a life, a triumph that should not continue into the next second. Grain, dust, and expression stay.

Sound may keep running (voiceover, a song, a crowd) so the freeze feels like a caption, not a crash. It is the wrong tool when you still need motion around a stopped body, or a camera that walks around an instant.

Those are frozen-in-motion and bullet time. A posed tableau with living extras is not a freeze.

Do not freeze a line of dialogue whose meaning is in the next word.

How it works

Select one frame and reprint or hold it for the required duration. An optical zoom into that still (as at the end of The 400 Blows) is a move on a photograph, not new live action.

The shutter is no longer sampling. Prompt: Freeze frame on [Subject], the world stopping on a decisive pose, grain holding, a still torn out of time.

When to use it

Use it to end, to joke, or to offer evidence, such as a final still of a runaway on a beach. Do not use it when particles should hang while the camera still travels.

Compared with similar shots

A freeze is not Slow Motion, which continues to sample the action, only slower. It is not Frozen in Motion, where a chosen person or the camera may still move while the world holds.

It is not Bullet Time, an orbit around a sculpture of speed. A Tableau is staged stillness inside living time, extras breathing, not a held frame.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

TableauHold the arrangement.

Fast MotionToo much life for real time.

In film

The 400 Blows ends on Antoine at the water, the image arrested so the boy cannot run farther. Goodfellas freezes Henry so voiceover can label a life mid-gesture.

Rocky is often cited for punctuation energy around a still of triumph. Trainspotting is listed beside freeze grammar more for its opening jolt than for a single copied hold.

Goodfellas 1990The Layla piano passage accompanies the discovery montage.

Trainspotting 1996The opening running sequence uses a prominent song cue.

Prompt it

Write a hold, not a slow pose. Still: the chosen frame as a photograph with grain, a decisive expression or body shape, no implied smear.

Video: Action around [Subject] freezes into a still frame and holds. Camera stops.

No orbit, no hanging debris that later falls.

Use in Video Generator

Edit a group of exhausted friends leaving an all-night diner at sunrise to an original energetic rock cue. Let the first strong beat land on the door opening, then allow the song to continue over several distinct street moments. Use a newly composed track, not a replica of an existing film song.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Frozen in Motion or Bullet Time. The tell is rain or coat tails hanging while the viewpoint keeps traveling, or a mid-air sculpture with parallax.

Fix: stop the camera and the world on one frame. If you need a walk around the instant, change technique.

Questions

What is Freeze Frame in film?

A freeze frame is a held still taken from the moving picture, so story time stops on one image.

Freeze Frame vs Frozen in Motion

A freeze holds the entire picture, camera included. Frozen in motion stops most of the world while a chosen body or the viewpoint may continue.

When should I use Freeze Frame?

When the still is the point: an ending, a joke, or a face presented as evidence. Let sound carry if the hold needs a caption.

How do I prompt Freeze Frame for AI image or video?

Write that action freezes into one still and holds, grain included, camera stopped. Ban orbits, hanging debris, and continued footsteps.

entries.title: Time-Lapse
entries.text:
Time-Lapse

Interval photographyTime compression

Time-lapse cinematography captures frames at long intervals so slow change plays as continuous motion, hours becoming seconds as shadows sweep and crowds become flow. It is interval photography, not a sped-up ordinary take.

Volume

Create this Time-Lapse

Narrative function

Use it to reveal a pattern no one can stand still long enough to see. Weather, construction, traffic, a plant, a city emptying and filling.

People often stop being protagonists and become a system. The camera is usually locked so the only motion is time.

It is the wrong tool for a comic undercrank of a performance, or for a still hero in a racing crowd (that is a different recipe). If the camera must walk the street while hours collapse, you wanted a hyperlapse.

Do not call a fast crowd under a stuck sun a full day-to-night lapse.

How it works

Plan interval, total duration, exposure, and stability. A locked head is the default.

For day-to-night, ramp exposure so windows light as the sky dies. The sun and shadows must travel if the claim is a full day.

Prompt: Time-lapse of [Subject] or the world around them, hours in seconds, shadows sweeping, crowds as smoke.

When to use it

Use it to show weather, construction, or a night becoming morning from a stable viewpoint. Do not use it to make an actor's performance merely faster.

Compared with similar shots

Time-lapse is not Fast Motion, which accelerates a continuous take. Hyperlapse adds significant camera travel through space on top of the interval.

Timelapse Landscape is the weather-and-shadow specialty. Timelapse Human freezes one will inside a racing crowd.

Timelapse Glam interval-samples wardrobe on a held face.

HyperlapseShow duration as velocity.

Fast MotionToo much life for real time.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

In film

Koyaanisqatsi turns traffic, crowds, and urban cycles into large-scale patterns. Baraka organizes cities and ritual through altered temporal scales.

Both are grammar for interval sampling, not frames to copy.

Koyaanisqatsi 1982Traffic, crowds and urban cycles become large-scale patterns.

Baraka 1992Cities and human activity are organized through altered temporal scales.

Prompt it

Name the interval collapse and what must move. Still: matched architecture at one implied phase, or a composite of sun angles only if you label it a study.

Video: Time-lapse around [Subject], light and crowds moving at accelerated speed while the camera stays or moves slowly. Shadows must travel.

Buildings stay solid.

Use in Video Generator

Locked high view of a public square from early morning to night, compressed into ten seconds. Shadows move continuously, crowds form and dissolve, windows light up gradually. Stable buildings and weather logic, no morphing architecture. Generate controlled day-phase keyframes and assemble a time-lapse progression.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Fast Motion. The tell is smeared pedestrians under a sun that never moves, or architecture that morphs.

Fix: write hours in seconds, a stable camera, and continuous shadow travel. If only people race, you have not shown a day.

Questions

What is Time-Lapse in film?

Time-lapse is interval photography: widely spaced frames played continuously so slow processes occupy a short passage.

Time-Lapse vs Fast Motion

Fast motion speeds a continuous recording. Time-lapse skips long stretches between frames, which is how a day, a build, or a sky can play in seconds.

When should I use Time-Lapse?

When the story is a process too slow for real time: weather, construction, crowds as flow, night becoming morning.

How do I prompt Time-Lapse for AI image or video?

Write hours in seconds, sweeping shadows, and a stable viewpoint. Require the sun to move if you claim a full day. Do not only speed a crowd.

entries.title: Step Printing
entries.text:
Step Printing

Repeated-frame motionWong Kar-wai motion texture

Step printing repeats or omits frames optically or digitally so motion advances in visible temporal steps. Combined with low-rate capture and long exposures, each frame smears internally while the sequence stutters forward, a texture of delay rather than clean high-frame-rate slow motion.

Volume

Create this Step Printing

Narrative function

Use it for longing that cannot move at normal speed: a walk through rain, a pursuit that feels remembered, a figure isolated from a city's rush. The smear belongs inside the frame.

The step belongs between frames. Together they make memory feel unstable without a digital glitch overlay.

It is the wrong tool for a readable impact study, a fight that must stay mechanical, or anxiety that should skip like a damaged mind. Those are slow motion and stutter.

Do not interpolate the cadence away. If the walk becomes silk, you left the technique.

How it works

Shoot or generate a low temporal sample (often well below 24 fps) with enough shutter time for motion blur, then duplicate frames to the delivery rate. Test the cadence.

Keep practical lights saturated and the lonely figure more readable than the crowd. Prompt: Step-printed motion of [Subject], frames duplicated, stuttering lyric delay, long-exposure smear inside each frame.

When to use it

Use it on a rain walk or a night counter where one person should separate from the city's rush. Do not use it when you need clean 120 fps anatomy of a hit.

Compared with similar shots

Step printing is not silk Slow Motion, which samples densely and interpolates smoothly. It is not Stutter / Stop-Stutter, which drops or repeats frames as anxious rhythm without requiring long-exposure smear.

Motion Blur can exist at normal cadence. Stop Motion builds poses by hand between exposures rather than reprinting live action.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

Stutter / Stop-StutterThe mind skips.

Fast MotionToo much life for real time.

In film

Chungking Express gives crowded street movement a blurred, stuttering temporal texture. Fallen Angels uses irregular urban motion and smear as a lonely gait.

In the Mood for Love is often remembered as slow romance. Much of that delay is step-printed texture rather than overcranked silk.

Chungking Express 1994Crowded street movement and pursuit have a blurred, stuttering temporal texture.

Fallen Angels 1995Urban passages use expressive irregular motion and blur.

Prompt it

Ask for duplicated frames and in-frame smear, not 120 fps. Still: a readable figure with strongly smeared passersby, long-exposure street texture.

Video: Step-printed slow motion of [Subject], stuttering duplicated frames, lyrical delay rather than smooth slow-mo. No generic glitch, no interpolated in-betweens.

Use in Video Generator

A lonely man stands at a night food counter while pedestrians stream past as smeared, stuttering shapes. His small movements remain readable. Long-exposure motion texture with deliberate repeated-frame cadence, saturated practical lights, no clean high-frame-rate slow motion. Apply the cadence in post from a controlled base clip.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Slow Motion. The tell is clean high-frame-rate motion with no step and no smear, or a datamosh overlay.

Fix: specify low-rate capture, long shutter, duplicated frames, and a cadence you can count.

Questions

What is Step Printing in film?

Step printing repeats or skips frames, often after low-rate long-exposure capture, so motion smears inside frames and advances in steps.

Step Printing vs Slow Motion

Slow motion is dense temporal sampling played slowly and smoothly. Step printing is a stepped, smeared cadence made by reprinting frames.

When should I use Step Printing?

When a walk, a pursuit, or a night street should feel like delayed memory rather than inspected physics.

How do I prompt Step Printing for AI image or video?

Write duplicated frames, stuttering lyric delay, and long-exposure smear. Forbid smooth 120 fps slow motion and generic digital glitches.

entries.title: Reverse Motion
entries.text:
Reverse Motion

Consequences before causes

Reverse motion plays recorded action backward so causes arrive after their effects inside the shot: rain rises, smoke inhales, a shattered object reassembles. This is reversed playback, not a story told in reverse scene order.

Volume

Create this Reverse Motion

Narrative function

Use it for trick photography, grief that wants an undo, or a world whose physics run the other way. The audience reads inverted inertia: water, cloth, sparks, and footsteps all lie.

A single reversed gesture can feel like a spell. A whole reversed fight can feel like entropy running downhill in the wrong direction.

It is the wrong tool when you only need a toy loop, or when the plot itself is told from consequence to cause without reversing the footage. A boomerang goes forward then back on the same path.

Memento-style chronology reorders scenes at normal playback. Do not mix those machines in one prompt.

How it works

Shoot the action forward with readable contacts, then reverse the clip. Gravity, fluids, and cloth are the proof.

A person putting on a coat forward will look like an impossible undressing in reverse only if the fabric was honest on the way in. Prompt: Reverse motion of [Subject], time running backward, rain rising, a broken thing assembling.

When to use it

Use it when a broken object should reassemble, or rain should rise, as a visible undo. Do not use it to mean reverse story order with ordinary-speed scenes.

Compared with similar shots

Reverse playback is not reverse chronology. Boomerang runs the same action forward then back as a loop.

Slow Motion only changes rate, not direction. An Infinite Loop sews last frame to first and may stay forward.

Tenet mixes inverted world-lines with true reversed footage. Memento and Irréversible mostly reorder scenes.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

Fast MotionToo much life for real time.

Speed RampMark one instant inside a fight or a look.

In film

Tenet lets objects and people move through events against the local clock, including true reversed photography. Cocteau's Orphée and related trick shots reverse ordinary gestures so they read as rites.

Memento opens with a Polaroid and a violent action running backward, then tells much of the rest by reverse scene order. Irréversible presents major sections from later to earlier without reversing every shot.

Memento 2000The color sequences move backward in story order, interwoven with forward-moving monochrome material.

Irréversible 2002The story’s major sections are presented in reverse order.

Memento 2000The opening Polaroid and violent action run backward.

Tenet 2020Objects and people can move through events in reverse temporal direction.

Prompt it

Name inverted physics, not a shuffled outline. Still: a tell such as rain hanging upward, glass mid-reassembly, smoke drawing in.

Video: The action around [Subject] plays in reverse: rain rising, smoke inhaling, motion undone. Ordinary-speed scenes in reverse order is a different brief.

Use in Video Generator

Create four ordinary-speed scenes about a broken friendship: an unopened apology, a public argument, a misunderstood message and an earlier act of trust. Present them in reverse chronological order. At each transition, reveal a cause that changes the previous scene’s meaning. Do not run the footage backward.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is reverse chronology or a Boomerang. The tell is a normal-speed scene shuffle, or a clip that goes forward then snaps back.

Fix: reverse one recorded action and show fluids, cloth, or debris traveling the wrong way along a single path.

Questions

What is Reverse Motion in film?

Reverse motion is recorded action played backward, so inertia, fluids, and contacts run from effect toward cause inside the shot.

Reverse Motion vs Reverse Chronology

Reverse motion rewinds the footage. Reverse chronology (Memento, Irréversible) reorders ordinary-speed scenes from consequence to cause.

When should I use Reverse Motion?

When the picture itself must undo physics: rising rain, assembling wreckage, a gesture that should feel like a reversed rite.

How do I prompt Reverse Motion for AI image or video?

Write time running backward with rain rising and smoke inhaling. Say the clip is reversed. Do not ask for shuffled scene order unless that is the job.

entries.title: Bullet Time
entries.text:
Bullet Time

Time-slice orbitThe Matrix effect

Bullet time freezes or radically slows action while the viewpoint travels around it, decoupling camera speed from subject time. The instant becomes inspectable space: a time-slice orbit around a sculpture of speed, not ordinary slow motion with a handheld camera.

Volume

Create this Bullet Time

Narrative function

Use it when a split-second decision should become architecture. The audience seems to occupy a viewpoint no observer inside the event could have.

Debris, rain, and coat tails hang so we can walk around them. The path is one move, usually an arc.

It is the wrong tool for a dinner scene, a lyric walk, or a simple impact study from a locked camera. If the camera is locked, you wanted frozen in motion or a freeze.

If the fighter keeps moving at stretched rate and the camera stays put, you wanted slow motion. Do not add a zoom on top of the orbit unless you are making a different shot.

How it works

Use a synchronized or time-offset multi-camera array with interpolation, or a fully controlled 3D scene. Enforce frozen or near-frozen subject geometry while changing viewpoint.

Particles should be countable and rigid enough to survive the arc. Prompt: Bullet time around [Subject], the moment frozen while the camera orbits, a slice of time as a sculpture.

When to use it

Use it to inspect an impact, a leap, or a dodge that already happened, as on a rooftop lean under gunfire. Do not use it as slow motion with a shaky camera.

Compared with similar shots

Bullet time is not Slow Motion, which stretches action without requiring a traveling viewpoint around a hold. It is not a normal 360-Degree Orbit, which circles living time.

It is not Freeze Frame, which stops the camera too. Frozen in Motion may let a chosen person move through a stopped world.

Bullet time stops or crushes the event while the camera walks around it.

360-Degree OrbitTime collapses around one person: kiss, threat, or product hero.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

Fast MotionToo much life for real time.

In film

The Matrix rooftop, Neo leaning under gunfire, is the textbook array move. Wanted curves bullets as inspectable paths through space.

Later action films borrow the split between body-time and camera-time. Prompt the physics, not a trademark.

The Matrix 1999Neo leans backward under gunfire on the rooftop.

Prompt it

Write two clocks: action stopped or crushed, camera continuing on a path. Still: one instant seen as if from a step along an orbit, hanging debris, consistent anatomy.

Video: Time freezes around [Subject] while the camera orbits, a bullet-time array move. No handheld slow-mo, no lock-off freeze.

Use in Video Generator

A dancer is suspended at the peak of a leap while loose paper hangs around her. The camera moves smoothly through a 90-degree arc at normal viewing speed while the leap advances only slightly. Consistent anatomy, rigid paper shapes, coherent shadows, no repeated body limbs. Build with multi-view keyframes or 3D for control.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is handheld Slow Motion. The tell is a moving fighter and a camera that does not orbit, or a freeze with no parallax.

Fix: subject frozen or nearly frozen, camera orbits a named arc, debris hanging, consistent shadows.

Questions

What is Bullet Time in film?

Bullet time is a viewpoint traveling around an event that is frozen or radically slowed, so camera speed and subject time are no longer the same clock.

Bullet Time vs Slow Motion

Slow motion stretches the action. Bullet time nearly stops the action and moves the camera around it, often with an array or a 3D reconstruction.

When should I use Bullet Time?

When a split-second must be inspected as space: a dodge, a leap, an impact the audience should walk around.

entries.title: Long Take
entries.text:
Long Take

plan sequenceextended takelong-duration shottrue long takesimulated long takeThe Atonement beach tableau

Long take cinematography is an unusually extended shot that preserves continuous performance, space, action, or duration without an overt cut. Blocking and camera share one sentence so the audience cannot leave the room.

Volume

Create this Long Take

Narrative function

Use it when incompatible facts must coexist in one geography: boredom beside danger, a joke beside a wound, a bomb in a trunk while people chat. The eye scans a functioning world instead of consuming an insert.

Duration is the tension. A dense crowd is not enough.

Each zone needs an intelligible action timed to the camera. It is the wrong tool when the scene is a virtuoso ride that may hide joins, or when coverage should isolate a face.

A oner is designed to play as one take and may be stitched. A long take's claim is continuous time.

Do not hold a static close-up for two minutes and call the endurance a panorama.

How it works

Block foreground, midground, and background on a shared timeline. Give the camera a clear route (Steadicam, crane, handheld, or studio dolly) and vary its attention without losing the human anchor.

Rehearse contacts, eyelines, and extra business so the take can survive. Prompt: Long take covering [Subject] without a cut, duration as tension, blocking and camera choreographed as one sentence.

When to use it

Use it when the audience must stay in the room, such as a car that cannot cut away from incoming gunfire. Do not use it to show off a corridor walk with nothing happening in depth.

Compared with similar shots

A long take emphasizes continuous duration. A Oner is designed to play without visible edits and may hide stitches.

Steadicam is a support, not a duration claim. An Invisible Cut is how some oners cheat.

A Master Shot covers the action so the scene can be cut. A long take often is the scene.

OnerThe scene is a ride.

SteadicamLong connecting moves through architecture. Neither handheld nor dolly.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

In film

Children of Men keeps car and birth passages inside continuous danger. The Player opens by walking conversations across a studio lot in one moving sentence.

Touch of Evil follows a bomb car while nearby people remain unaware. Atonement's Dunkirk beach moves among soldiers, wreckage, and stranded activity.

Russian Ark and Victoria extend the wager to feature length.

Atonement 2007The Dunkirk beach passage moves among soldiers, wreckage and stranded activity.

The Player 1992The opening moves between conversations across the studio lot.

Touch of Evil 1958The opening follows a car after a bomb is placed in its trunk, while nearby people remain unaware.

Russian Ark 2002The journey through the Hermitage is presented as one continuous feature-length take.

Victoria 2015The night out and subsequent events unfold in a continuous feature-length take.

Prompt it

Write unbroken duration and what happens in depth. Still: a wide ensemble with a readable route, not proof of a take.

Video: An unbroken long take following [Subject] through the space with no cut. Name foreground, midground, and background actions on one timeline.

No disaster spectacle; distinct actions continue independently in depth. Keep the nurse as a loose visual anchor.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a stitched Oner sold as uncut truth, or a crowded wide with no timed business. The tell is a whip into darkness, a crossing truck, or extras who only occupy space.

Fix: one overt take, distinct actions in depth, a camera route, and a human anchor.

Questions

What is Long Take in film?

A long take is an unusually extended shot that keeps performance, space, and duration continuous without an overt cut.

Long Take vs Oner

A long take claims continuous recorded time. A oner is designed to play as one take and may include invisible stitches as long as the joins do not read.

When should I use Long Take?

When leaving the room would leak tension, and the world in depth must keep working around the people we follow.

entries.title: Oner
entries.text:
Oner

true onerstitched oner

A oner shot is designed to play as if the scene were one take, with no visible edits. It may be a true single take or a stitched oner whose joins hide in whips, darkness, or crossing bodies.

Volume

Create this Oner

Narrative function

Use it when geography, breath, and choreography should feel like one continuous push: a backstage spiral, a trench, an extraction through apartments. Hidden cuts are allowed only if they are invisible.

The audience should not be able to point to the splice. The camera and the blocking are one machine.

It is the wrong tool when the ethical claim is uncut duration, or when the scene is a quiet two-person talk that only needs a master. A true long take refuses the stitch.

A oner may use it. Do not call three coverage angles a oner because the editor was smooth.

How it works

Choreograph a path that can be performed, then decide where a join could hide if the take cannot be true. Steadicam, crane, and handheld all work if the breath stays consistent.

Match lighting and eyelines across stitches. Prompt: Apparent oner of [Subject], a whole scene as one take, hidden cuts allowed only if invisible.

When to use it

Use it when the scene is a ride through connected actions, such as a backstage spiral or a trench crossing. Do not use it for a static conversation that only needs coverage.

Compared with similar shots

A Long Take emphasizes uncut duration as a fact. A oner emphasizes the ride and may be stitched.

Steadicam is often the support. An Invisible Cut is the join.

Tracking Shot and Follow Shot can exist inside a oner without making every track a oner.

Long TakeDo not let the audience leave the room.

SteadicamLong connecting moves through architecture. Neither handheld nor dolly.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

In film

Birdman plays backstage panic as one apparent breath, stitches hidden. 1917 connects trench and field into a continuous war path, also stitched.

Extraction runs apartment and vehicle action as a designed single-take sequence. Compare those with Russian Ark, a true feature-length take, if the claim is uncut fact rather than ride.

Prompt it

Write a whole scene as one take. Still: a frame from the path, not proof.

Video: A continuous oner following [Subject] through connected actions without a visible cut. Name rooms, turns, and the human anchor.

Hidden cuts only if they would not read.

A continuous oner following [Subject] through connected actions without a visible cut.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is ordinary coverage, or a Long Take you secretly cut. The tell is a change of breath, a jump in extra positions, or a whip that does not match.

Fix: one visible path, matched energy across any hidden join, and no insert that admits the splice.

Questions

What is Oner in film?

A oner is a shot designed to play without visible edits, whether it is a true single take or a stitched sequence whose joins do not read.

Oner vs Long Take

A long take is continuous recorded duration. A oner is the ride: it can be true or stitched, as long as the audience cannot see the cut.

When should I use Oner?

When the scene should feel like one breath through connected spaces and actions, and coverage would leak the charge.

entries.title: Motion Blur
entries.text:
Motion Blur

Motion blur cinematography is the streaking or softness caused by subject or camera movement during exposure. The longer the gate stays open relative to the motion, the more the image paints, so edges fail on purpose.

Volume

Create this Motion Blur

Narrative function

Use it when speed or trauma should smear: headlights as ribbons, a body that cannot be counted, a whip that erases geography for a frame. Normal 180-degree film already has some blur.

This look commits further, so edges fail on purpose. It is the wrong tool for staccato combat that should feel like discrete fragments.

That is short shutter, often misfiled under the same war films. Slow motion with dense samples can look sharper, not smearier.

Do not add a blur overlay on a sharp take and call it shutter.

How it works

Expose long enough, or move fast enough, that edges streak within the frame. A Whip Pan is a burst of this.

A locked camera with a racing subject is the other axis. Night lamps help because they write ribbons.

Prompt: Long-shutter motion blur on [Subject] or the world, streaks of light, bodies smearing.

When to use it

Use it when a night street or a panicked camera move should smear, such as lamps dragging during a run. Do not use it when you want Saving Private Ryan's crisp, segmented droplets.

Compared with similar shots

Motion blur is smear from exposure. Low Shutter in this library is short shutter: reduced blur, staccato edges.

A Whip Pan is camera rotation fast enough to erase the middle. Slow Motion often looks sharper because each high-fps frame is a shorter exposure.

Step Printing smears and steps. Do not confuse photography's 'low shutter speed' with film's low shutter angle.

Whip PanTransition, punchline, or sudden attention shift.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

Fast MotionToo much life for real time.

In film

Cloverfield lets handheld panic smear the monster and the street. Whip-heavy action (the Bourne films among them) uses bursts of blur as geography fails.

Saving Private Ryan is often listed here, but Omaha Beach is largely short-shutter staccato, the cousin, not the smear.

Prompt it

Commit to streaks. Still: lamps as ribbons, bodies smearing, a subject sharp only if they held still.

Video: Heavy motion blur as [Subject] or the camera moves, light streaking, shutter dragged. If every raindrop is crisp, the shutter was too short.

Use in Video Generator

Heavy motion blur as [Subject] or the camera moves, light streaking, shutter dragged.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Low Shutter (short shutter angle). The tell is crispy rain and chopped limbs with no ribbons.

Fix: drag the shutter or increase motion until lights streak. If you wanted SPR cadence, change technique rather than adding a blur filter.

Questions

What is Motion Blur in film?

Motion blur is streaking or softness from subject or camera movement while the shutter is open. It is exposure plus velocity, not a separate object.

Motion Blur vs Low Shutter

Motion blur is smear from a longer exposure relative to movement. Low shutter here means a short shutter angle: sharper, staccato frames with less blur.

When should I use Motion Blur?

When speed or trauma should paint: night lamps as ribbons, a whip that erases the middle, a body that cannot be counted.

How do I prompt Motion Blur for AI image or video?

Write long-shutter streaks, dragging lights, and smearing bodies. Demand that raindrops and limbs are not all crisp.

entries.title: Stutter / Stop-Stutter
entries.text:
Stutter / Stop-Stutter

Stutter editing drops or repeats frames so playback skips and the world's clock hitches. It is an anxious rhythm, not the lyric smear of step printing and not a jump cut's spatial jump.

Volume

Create this Stutter / Stop-Stutter

Narrative function

Use it when thought itself is damaged: obsession, panic, a headache that cuts time into chips. The picture may stay in the same setup while frames go missing or repeat.

Cadence is the meaning. A little is a twitch.

A lot is a seizure. It is the wrong tool for Wong Kar-wai rain, for Godard-style discontinuous geography, or for stop-motion craft.

If the smear is romantic, you wanted step printing. If the camera angle or body position jumps, you wanted a jump cut.

Do not add a codec glitch unless the story is a broken file.

How it works

Start from a clean take, then remove or duplicate frames on a planned irregular grid. You can also skip in camera by lowering sample rate without long-exposure smear.

Keep identity and space continuous so the hitch reads as time, not as a cut. Prompt: Stuttered motion of [Subject], frames dropping or repeating, a glitch in time, anxiety as rhythm.

When to use it

Use it when a thought or a panic attack should skip, such as a close face whose blinks do not land on a steady clock. Do not use it as lyric street texture.

Compared with similar shots

Stutter is not Step Printing, which reprints long-exposure frames into a smeared delay. It is not a Jump Cut, which discards time and often shows a spatial jump in the same setup.

Stop Motion is pose-to-pose craft. Datamosh is compression damage.

Keep them separate in the prompt.

Step PrintingLonging that cannot move at normal speed.

Jump CutDo not soothe. Show the skip.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

In film

Pi uses staccato, high-contrast skipping so numbers and pain share a rhythm. Music videos often stutter a gesture as a beat.

Aronofsky's later montage grammar (Requiem among them) neighbors this hitch without being identical to skip-frame stutter.

Prompt it

Write frames dropping or repeating, not smear and not a jump in angle. Still: a face or gesture that looks temporally sampled, slight after-images only if they come from repeats.

Video: Stuttering playback of [Subject], frames repeating and skipping, anxious rhythm. Same setup, no lyric blur, no datamosh.

Use in Video Generator

Stuttering playback of [Subject], frames repeating and skipping, anxious rhythm.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Step Printing or Jump Cut. The tell is romantic long-exposure crowds, or a sudden change of body position that reads as an edit.

Fix: keep space continuous and make the cadence irregular. Count the missing frames.

Questions

What is Stutter / Stop-Stutter in film?

Stutter is playback that drops or repeats frames so time hitches. The setup usually stays put while the clock skips.

Stutter vs Step Printing

Step printing is smeared, lyric, duplicated-frame delay. Stutter is anxious skip-or-repeat rhythm without requiring long-exposure texture.

When should I use Stutter?

When panic, obsession, or pain should make the mind skip. Keep the same setup so the hitch is temporal.

How do I prompt Stutter for AI image or video?

Write frames repeating and skipping, anxious rhythm, same camera setup. Forbid smooth slow motion, romantic smear, and jump-cut geography.

entries.title: Boomerang
entries.text:
Boomerang

A boomerang video effect plays a short action forward, then snaps it backward along the same samples, often looping. The gesture comes and goes on one path: reversed playback used as a round trip rather than a one-way undo.

Volume

Create this Boomerang

Narrative function

Use it to weaponize a small motion: hair toss, splash, a jump's peak, a door that never finishes closing. Both directions must read.

If the forward pass is ugly, the reverse will not save it. Loops work when the end of the reverse meets the start of the forward without a bump.

It is the wrong tool for grief, inverted physics as story, or a seamless forward-only cycle (a pendulum designed to sew). Reverse motion one way is a spell.

An infinite loop may never reverse. Do not boomerang a line of dialogue whose words cannot run backward.

How it works

Record a short, readable gesture with clean contacts, play it forward, then reverse the same frames. Trim so the join is at a still-ish peak or a matched pose.

Camera usually locked. Prompt: Boomerang of [Subject], action running forward then snapping backward on the same path, a loop of coming and going.

When to use it

Use it to turn a splash, a jump, or a hair toss into a toy loop. Do not use it for a one-way undo of a crash.

Compared with similar shots

A boomerang is not one-way Reverse Motion. It is not an Infinite Loop that sews last frame to first while staying forward.

A Moonwalk is a body's lie in living time. A Cinemagraph freezes most of a still and loops one element.

Infinite LoopDuration without progress.

Reverse MotionMagic, grief, or a world with inverted physics.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

In film

Instagram and Vine made the round-trip native. Music videos use it as a hook on a single gesture.

Feature grammar rarely needs it except as a quoted phone-screen or a title-card gag.

Prompt it

Write the round trip. Still: the mid-gesture peak, because a still cannot boomerang.

Video: [Subject] plays forward then reverses along the same motion, a seamless boomerang loop. Same path, no new action on the way back, no one-way reverse.

Use in Video Generator

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Reverse Motion or a forward Infinite Loop. The tell is rain that only rises, or a loop that never rewinds.

Fix: specify forward then back on the same samples, and a join that matches.

Questions

What is Boomerang in film?

A boomerang plays a short action forward and then backward on the same path, often as a loop, so the gesture comes and goes.

Boomerang vs Reverse Motion

Reverse motion rewinds once and stays in that direction. A boomerang is a round trip: forward, then back, usually repeating.

When should I use Boomerang?

When a small physical gesture should become a toy: splash, jump, toss. Both directions must remain readable.

How do I prompt Boomerang for AI image or video?

entries.title: Infinite Loop
entries.text:
Infinite Loop

Repeated dayIterative narrative

An infinite loop video sews the last frame to the first so motion never arrives at an ending. The cycle can be a seamless visual join, or, in narrative use, a repeated day whose variables change.

Volume

Create this Infinite Loop

Narrative function

As a picture machine, design a motion whose end state matches its start: position, light, pose. The cut should vanish.

As a story machine, repeat an event sequence while knowledge or one decision changes. Those are cousins that share a name.

Do not prompt them as one blob. It is the wrong tool for a forward-back toy (boomerang) or a mostly still image with one living detail (cinemagraph).

A loop that changes everything at once has no baseline. A join that flashes is just a cut.

How it works

For a visual loop, match the first and last frames and keep the action forward. For a narrative loop, establish a reset cue and a stable baseline, then vary a small number of actions per cycle.

Prompt: Infinite loop of [Subject], the last frame sewing to the first, a motion that never arrives.

When to use it

Use it when a motion or a day should fail to conclude, such as a walk cycle that sews or a morning that resets. Do not use it when you want a boomerang snap.

Compared with similar shots

An infinite loop is not a Boomerang, which rewinds the same samples. A Cinemagraph holds a still and loops one island of motion.

Reverse Motion is direction, not a sew. Narrative loops (Groundhog Day) change behavior inside a repeated event.

Visual loops must match ends.

BoomerangTurn a gesture into a toy.

CinemagraphA photograph that refuses to die.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

In film

GIF culture and installation video are the visual grammar: a motion that can play forever. Groundhog Day returns the same morning while Phil's behavior changes.

Run Lola Run repeats attempts with varied actions and outcomes. Edge of Tomorrow turns repetition into training.

Groundhog Day 1993The same morning returns while Phil’s behavior changes.

Run Lola Run 1998Repeated attempts vary actions and outcomes.

Edge of Tomorrow 2014Repeated experience produces learned adaptations.

Prompt it

Say whether you want a seamless visual sew or a repeated-day story. Still: a pose that could be both start and end.

Video: A seamless loop of [Subject], end matching start, no cut visible. Forward motion unless you explicitly want a boomerang.

Use in Video Generator

Design three repetitions of a commuter’s morning: the same alarm, dropped coin and departing bus. In each cycle she changes one decision, producing a different encounter. Reuse matched camera positions and reset sounds. Generate the baseline once, then controlled variations with stable people and geography.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Boomerang. The tell is a visible rewind, or a reset with no matching frames.

Fix: match last frame to first, keep direction consistent, and change only the variables you mean to change.

Questions

What is Infinite Loop in film?

An infinite loop either sews last frame to first so a motion never ends, or repeats an event sequence while knowledge or choices change.

Infinite Loop vs Boomerang

A boomerang runs forward then backward on the same path. A visual infinite loop usually stays forward and matches its ends so the join vanishes.

When should I use Infinite Loop?

When duration should not progress: a seamless cycle, or a repeated day that makes one changed decision comparable.

How do I prompt Infinite Loop for AI image or video?

Write a seamless loop, end matching start, no visible cut. If you mean a repeated-day story, say the reset cue and what changes each cycle.

entries.title: Stop Motion
entries.text:
Stop Motion

Frame-by-frame object animationReplacement animation

Stop motion cinematography photographs physical objects incrementally, adjusting them between exposures so successive poses create apparent movement. The cadence is pose to pose and slightly staccato, with tactile materials in the light.

Volume

Create this Stop Motion

Narrative function

Use it when motion should feel made: puppets, replacement faces, dinosaurs that are sculptures, a fox whose fur is fabric. Weight, texture, and small irregularities are the performance.

Live-action smoothness would be the wrong world. It is the wrong tool for a choppy filter on a real actor, or for step-printed streets.

If the fox's fur flows like photographed animal hair, you left the craft. A generated 'stop-motion look' is an aesthetic.

Frame-by-frame production is a method. Say which one you want.

How it works

Lock the camera. Repeat the lighting.

Plan pose spacing. Secure the model so it does not drift.

Replacement animation swaps parts (mouths, lids) between frames. For generated approximations, specify consistent materials, visible joints, and deliberate increments.

Prompt: Stop-motion of [Subject], stepped poses, tactile increment, time built by hand.

When to use it

Use it when a puppet or object should perform as a photographed sculpture, such as a fox folding paper on a miniature desk. Do not use it as a jitter preset on live action.

Compared with similar shots

Stop motion is not Step Printing of live footage. It is a branch of Animation, specifically frame-by-frame object animation, including replacement animation.

Stutter / Stop-Stutter skip-frames living time. Low Shutter makes live action staccato without posing a model.

Step PrintingLonging that cannot move at normal speed.

AnimationThe world is constructed, not captured.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

In film

King Kong (1933) animates Kong and prehistoric creatures as physical models. Jason and the Argonauts combines Harryhausen figures with live action in the skeleton fight.

The Nightmare Before Christmas and Coraline perform with puppets and miniatures. Fantastic Mr.

Fox keeps tactile fur and handmade increment as the world's law.

King Kong 1933Kong and prehistoric creatures are animated as physical models.

Jason and the Argonauts 1963The skeleton fight combines animated figures and live action.

Coraline 2009Puppet performances and miniature environments.

Prompt it

Write materials and increments, not a filter. Still: a puppet or object mid-pose, visible construction, coherent joints.

Video: Stop-motion cadence of [Subject], pose to pose, slightly staccato. Stable lights and set, readable hand-object contact, no fluid live-action fur.

Use in Video Generator

An articulated paper-and-wire fox carefully folds a paper boat on a miniature desk. Tactile materials, consistent joint construction, deliberate frame-by-frame posing and small controlled increments. Stable lighting and set, readable hand-object contact, no fluid live-action fur or continuously melting paper.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a live-action jitter or Step Printing. The tell is morphing materials, melting paper, or continuously flowing hair.

Fix: consistent model, deliberate pose changes, locked camera, repeatable light.

Questions

What is Stop Motion in film?

Stop motion is frame-by-frame photography of adjusted objects or puppets, so their successive poses create movement.

Stop Motion vs Step Printing

Step printing reprints live-action frames into a smear-and-step cadence. Stop motion builds each frame by moving a physical (or consistent digital) model.

When should I use Stop Motion?

When the world should feel handmade: puppets, miniatures, objects that perform. Not when you only want live action to hitch.

How do I prompt Stop Motion for AI image or video?

Write stepped poses, tactile materials, pose-to-pose cadence, and a stable camera. Forbid fluid live-action motion and choppy-filter shortcuts.

entries.title: Low Shutter
entries.text:
Low Shutter

Crisp motion cadenceReduced motion blur

Low shutter cinematography uses a short shutter angle or short exposure so moving edges stay sharp inside each frame. Normal-rate action then feels abrupt and staccato because this is reduced motion blur, not a long-exposure smear.

Volume

Create this Low Shutter

Narrative function

Use it when impact and sensory stress should feel exposed: rain as beads, limbs as chopped positions, a landing that does not silk over. You are not speeding the scene.

You are removing the blur that usually glues fragments together. Combat and panic live here.

It is the wrong tool for night-traffic ribbons, lyric smear, or silk slow motion. Photography says 'low shutter speed' for long exposure.

Film says low shutter angle for the opposite. If every lamp paints a ribbon, you shot motion blur.

Do not skip frames and call that short shutter.

How it works

At 24 fps, a 180-degree shutter is about 1/48 s. A 45-degree shutter is about 1/192 s: less blur, more light required.

Compensate exposure. In generated footage, request low motion blur and crisp droplets, not missing frames.

Prompt: Low-shutter (short shutter angle) of [Subject], reduced motion blur, crisp rain and limb edges, staccato cadence.

When to use it

Use it on a landing, a rescue run, or a fight that should feel like discrete fragments, such as Omaha-style rain and bodies. Do not use it when lamps should drag as ribbons.

Compared with similar shots

Low shutter here is the inverse of Motion Blur. A Whip Pan smears by rotating fast, usually with a normal or long shutter.

Slow Motion can look sharp because high fps shortens each exposure, but the clock is stretched. Stutter / Stop-Stutter drops frames.

Short shutter, low frame rate, skipped frames, and speed changes are separate controls.

Motion BlurSpeed or trauma. Clarity would be false.

Whip PanTransition, punchline, or sudden attention shift.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

In film

Saving Private Ryan's Omaha Beach landing is the grammar: sharp, harshly segmented movement. Gladiator uses aggressive, discontinuous-looking motion on selected battle images.

Cloverfield is listed nearby for chaos, but much of that chaos is handheld smear, the cousin.

Saving Private Ryan 1998The Omaha Beach landing has sharp, harshly segmented movement.

Gladiator 2000Selected battle imagery uses aggressive, discontinuous-looking motion treatment.

Prompt it

Adapt the catalog line toward the physics: short shutter, not long smear. Still: crisp droplets and defined moving limbs in a tense handheld frame.

Video: Handheld close action of [Subject], normal playback speed, short-exposure droplets, sharply segmented body movement, no smooth slow motion, no artificial frame skipping.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Motion Blur (and the phrase 'low shutter speed'). The tell is ribbons of light and unreadable rain.

Fix: specify short shutter angle or 1/200 s class exposure, reduced motion blur, staccato edges. If you wanted paint, go to motion blur.

Questions

What is Low Shutter in film?

Low shutter here means a short shutter angle: each frame is exposed briefly, so motion stays crisp and staccato instead of smeared.

Low Shutter vs Motion Blur

Motion blur streaks because the shutter stays open during movement. Low shutter angle cuts that blur so fragments of action stay sharp.

When should I use Low Shutter?

When a hit, a run, or a landing should feel like exposed fragments at normal speed, not like silk and not like night-traffic ribbons.

entries.title: Timelapse Glam
entries.text:
Timelapse Glam

Timelapse glam is interval photography of a styling process in which clothes, hair, and makeup change at high speed while the face holds. The person is a still axis and wardrobe is the changing weather.

Volume

Create this Timelapse Glam

Narrative function

Use it to show transformation as labor rather than as a cut to a new costume. Stylists swarm.

Hangers fly. Identity must survive the swarm or the face becomes a morph.

The camera is usually locked. The clock is the dressing room's, not the street's.

It is the wrong tool for landscape days, racing crowds, or a freeze of the world. If the city is the process, you wanted time-lapse or timelapse landscape.

If only the person is a statue in traffic, you wanted timelapse human. Do not let the skull drift.

How it works

Lock identity, eyeline, and camera. Interval-sample while wardrobe and hair change in discrete, readable steps.

Hands of stylists may smear. The face should not.

Prompt: Timelapse glam of [Subject], styling swarm, clothes and hair changing while the face holds.

When to use it

Use it when a look is assembled in public, such as a held face while stylists swap dresses at interval speed. Do not use it to time-lapse a skyline.

Compared with similar shots

This is a specialty of Time-Lapse, not a Glam lighting pattern alone. Timelapse Human holds a person while a crowd races.

Timelapse Landscape holds geography while weather races. A montage of costume changes with cuts is editing, not interval sampling.

Time-LapseShow weather, construction, or a night becoming morning.

GlamSell the face.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

In film

Vogue transformation films and fashion-week process pieces are the native grammar. Music videos use interval wardrobe bursts on a held star.

Feature films more often cut montages. If you need a narrative cousin, think process, not a copied title sequence.

Prompt it

Lock the face, accelerate the styling. Still: one held identity with evidence of process (hands, garments in mid-swap).

Video: Time-lapse around a still [Subject] as stylists and wardrobe change at high speed. Same skull, same eyeline, clothes as weather, no identity morph.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a costume Montage or a face morph. The tell is a changing skull, or a city time-lapse with no styling work.

Fix: hold identity and camera, interval the wardrobe, keep stylist hands as the swarm.

Questions

What is Timelapse Glam in film?

Timelapse glam interval-samples a styling session so clothes and hair change quickly while the face remains a stable identity.

Timelapse Glam vs Time-Lapse

Time-lapse is the parent interval method. Timelapse glam restricts it to a held person whose wardrobe and hair are the changing weather.

When should I use Timelapse Glam?

When transformation is the beat and should be seen as process: a look assembled, not a cut to a new costume.

How do I prompt Timelapse Glam for AI image or video?

Write a still face, a styling swarm, and clothes changing at high speed. Lock identity. Forbid morphing skulls and city-only lapses.

entries.title: Timelapse Human
entries.text:
Timelapse Human

Timelapse human holds one person in living time while the crowd is interval-sampled into smoke, so one still will stands in a rushing system. It is the opposite clock of a frozen world with a moving hero.

Volume

Create this Timelapse Human

Narrative function

Use it when isolation is a rate difference: the subject decides, waits, or grieves at 24 fps while the city is hours. Commuters become flow.

The camera is usually locked so the contrast stays readable. A tiny sway in the hero is allowed.

Walking at full speed through a lapse crowd breaks the contract. It is the wrong tool when the world should freeze and the hero should walk (frozen in motion), or when weather is the subject (timelapse landscape).

The Matrix lobby is often misfiled here. That lobby is bullet time: an orbit around a crushed instant, not interval crowds around a statue.

How it works

Lock the hero's mark and the camera. Sample passersby at long intervals, or composite a held performance over a crowd lapse.

Shadows on the hero should not travel like a full day unless that is the story. Prompt: Timelapse human of [Subject] frozen in a rushing crowd, people as smoke, one still will.

When to use it

Use it when one person should hold a station or a square while the crowd becomes smoke. Do not use it when that person must walk through a stopped city.

Compared with similar shots

This is Time-Lapse applied to extras around a held lead. Frozen in Motion freezes the crowd and lets the lead (or camera) move.

Bullet Time orbits a near-frozen event. Timelapse Landscape races weather, not pedestrians.

Fast Motion would accelerate the hero too.

Time-LapseShow weather, construction, or a night becoming morning.

Frozen in MotionStop the world, keep the pose.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

In film

Koyaanisqatsi turns crowds into systems. The still-person-in-racing-crowd recipe is a commercial and music-video cousin of that grammar.

The Matrix lobby stills are a frequent false reference. They belong with bullet time.

Prompt it

Hold the person, lapse the crowd. Still: one sharp figure, pedestrians as flow, stable sun unless you want a day.

Video: Crowds time-lapse around a still [Subject], the city racing, the person holding. No frozen pigeons, no orbit, no hero sprinting through stopped extras.

Use in Video Generator

Crowds time-lapse around a still [Subject], the city racing, the person holding.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Frozen in Motion or Bullet Time. The tell is stopped extras and a walking hero, or a camera orbit around hanging brass.

Fix: subject holds, crowd races, camera locked, people as smoke.

Questions

What is Timelapse Human in film?

Timelapse human keeps one person nearly still while interval-sampled crowds race around them, so isolation reads as a difference in clocks.

Timelapse Human vs Frozen in Motion

Timelapse human races the world around a held person. Frozen in motion stops the world so a chosen person or the camera can still move.

When should I use Timelapse Human?

When one will should stand while a station, lobby, or street becomes flow. The hero is the still axis.

How do I prompt Timelapse Human for AI image or video?

Write crowds time-lapsing around a still [Subject], people as smoke, camera locked. Forbid a walking hero in a frozen crowd and bullet-time orbits.

entries.title: Timelapse Landscape
entries.text:
Timelapse Landscape

Timelapse landscape interval-samples light and weather over a place so hours play in seconds as clouds and shadows sweep. Geography is the actor, and a person, if present, is a scale mark rather than a racing extra.

Volume

Create this Timelapse Landscape

Narrative function

Use it when the story is a sky, a desert, a city grid as climate, a ridge that must survive several suns. The camera is locked or on a slow, even move that does not fight the sun's path.

Buildings and rock stay solid. Clouds are the motion.

It is the wrong tool for wardrobe process, a still hero in a smoking crowd, or undercranked acting. If the camera walks the avenue in steps, you wanted a hyperlapse.

If only headlights streak under a stuck sun, you have not shown a landscape day.

How it works

Choose interval from the process (clouds faster than a shadow-day, stars slower). Lock off or use a motion-control pan.

Ramp exposure for day-to-night. Keep the sun's arc continuous.

Prompt: Timelapse landscape around [Subject] or their place, clouds and shadows sweeping, hours in seconds.

When to use it

Use it to show the day turning over a ridge, a square, or a citadel. Do not use it as a crowd recipe with a motionless sky.

Compared with similar shots

This is Time-Lapse aimed at weather and terrain. Aerial may carry it if the viewpoint is high, but height is not the interval.

Hyperlapse moves the camera through space in steps. Timelapse Human races people.

Fast Motion speeds a continuous take.

Time-LapseShow weather, construction, or a night becoming morning.

AerialOpen a world. Make the place bigger than the person.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

In film

Baraka and Koyaanisqatsi are the landscape-and-city interval grammar: clouds, shadows, and human systems at non-human rates. Later nature films inherit the same sun-and-cloud contract.

The still should imply a phase of day, not a morphing mountain.

Prompt it

Write light and weather as the motion. Still: one honest sun angle on stable geology.

Video: Time-lapse of light and weather over the landscape of [Subject]. Shadows sweep, clouds race, architecture holds.

No morphing cliffs, no crowd-only acceleration.

Use in Video Generator

Time-lapse of light and weather over the landscape of [Subject].

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Fast Motion or Timelapse Human. The tell is racing people under a stuck sun, or mountains that melt.

Fix: hours in seconds, traveling shadows, solid ground, camera stable or slowly authored.

Questions

What is Timelapse Landscape in film?

Timelapse landscape is interval photography of a place so weather, shadows, and sun travel occupy a short passage.

Timelapse Landscape vs Time-Lapse

Time-lapse is the method. Timelapse landscape restricts the subject to geography and climate, not wardrobe or a held pedestrian.

When should I use Timelapse Landscape?

When the day turning is the beat: clouds, shadows, night becoming morning over a stable place.

How do I prompt Timelapse Landscape for AI image or video?

Write hours in seconds, sweeping clouds and shadows, and solid geography. Require the sun to move. Do not only speed a crowd.

entries.title: Frozen in Motion
entries.text:
Frozen in Motion

Time-stop environment

Frozen in motion stops the environment and most people while a chosen character, the viewpoint, or both continue to move. Particles, extras, and pigeons hang, and the rule of who may move is the entire effect.

Volume

Create this Frozen in Motion

Narrative function

Use it to separate a mind from consequence: superhuman perception, a wish to step outside a square, a kitchen instant stretched into a walk. Julie can run through a stopped Oslo.

Quicksilver can work a room the rest of the world cannot occupy. Hair, weather, shadows, and loose objects must obey the same freeze or the illusion dies.

It is the wrong tool when the whole picture should hold (freeze-frame), when the camera should orbit a crushed event (bullet time), or when crowds should race around a statue (timelapse human). Do not freeze the hero and the street together unless you mean a still.

How it works

Decide the rule: extras hold, fluids and debris are suspended, the subject and/or camera may travel. Use held extras and practical supports for simple beats, VFX or 3D for complex hangs.

Prompt: Frozen-in-motion of [Subject], the world stopped mid-gesture, particles hanging, [Subject] or the camera still allowed to move.

When to use it

Use it when one person should walk a stopped street, or work a stopped kitchen, while pigeons and extras hang. Do not use it as a freeze of the entire frame, and do not race the crowd.

Compared with similar shots

Frozen in motion is not Freeze Frame (camera and world both stop). It is not Bullet Time (event crushed, camera orbits a sculpture).

It is not Timelapse Human (crowd races, hero holds). Slow Motion still advances everyone, only slower.

Keep the permission list explicit.

Bullet TimeA moment is so important it becomes architecture.

Freeze FrameEnd, joke, or evidence.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

In film

X-Men: Days of Future Past expands Quicksilver's Pentagon kitchen into a subjective instant the others cannot share. The Worst Person in the World lets Julie run through an Oslo whose other inhabitants are suspended.

The Matrix rooftop is the orbiting cousin, bullet time, not this split of who may walk.

X-Men: Days of Future Past 2014The Pentagon kitchen sequence expands Quicksilver’s subjective instant.

The Worst Person in the World 2021Julie runs through an Oslo whose other inhabitants are suspended.

Prompt it

Name who moves. Still: one active subject in a square of frozen pedestrians and hanging debris.

Video: Action around [Subject] freezes mid-move while [Subject] and/or the camera may still travel. Coherent suspended poses, no breathing crowds, no racing extras, no array orbit unless you actually want bullet time.

Use in Video Generator

A woman walks through a city square where all other people are motionless mid-gesture and pigeons hang in the air. Only she, her clothing and the following camera move. Coherent suspended poses, no breathing crowds, no melting birds, quiet suspended mood.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Freeze Frame, Bullet Time, or Timelapse Human. The tell is a fully still picture, an orbit around a statue, or people as smoke.

Fix: write the freeze rule, hang the extras, and let only the chosen body or camera continue.

Questions

What is Frozen in Motion in film?

Frozen in motion stops most of the world while a chosen person and/or the camera keep moving, so one clock splits from the rest.

Frozen in Motion vs Bullet Time

Bullet time walks the camera around a nearly frozen event. Frozen in motion lets a character inhabit a stopped world, not only inspect it from an orbit.

When should I use Frozen in Motion?

When one person's experience should leave the world's clock: a run through a stopped city, a superhuman chore in a held kitchen.

How do I prompt Frozen in Motion for AI image or video?

Write a stopped environment, hanging particles, and a clear permission: who may move. Ban a full freeze, a racing crowd, and an array orbit unless you want those cousins.

entries.title: Moonwalk
entries.text:
Moonwalk

A moonwalk effect is a backward glide that reads as a forward myth: the torso stays upright, one foot slides, the other pushes, and the heel does not lift like a walk. It is a locomotion lie in living time, not reversed footage.

Volume

Create this Moonwalk

Narrative function

Use it when gait itself is the spectacle: dance, a villain who does not obey floors, a sidewalk that should feel like ice. Wet asphalt or a stage helps the read.

Coat tails should trail the slide, not bounce like steps. It is the wrong tool for a chase on gravel, a grief undo, or a toy loop.

Reverse motion would rewind the whole world. A boomerang would come and go.

A double dolly puts subject and camera on one platform so the world slides while the walk may be ordinary. Moonwalk is the body's lie.

Do not also spin or levitate.

How it works

Write a backward slide, upright torso, one foot gliding, the other pushing. Camera can lock or track laterally.

Keep contact with the floor. Prompt: Moonwalk of [Subject], backward glide that reads as forward myth, slide as dance grammar.

When to use it

Use it when the walk is the trick, such as a backward glide on wet night asphalt. Do not use it as reversed footage of an ordinary walk.

Compared with similar shots

A moonwalk is not Reverse Motion of a forward walk (that inverts the whole street). It is not a Boomerang loop.

A Double Dolly can fake a similar float by moving person and camera together, world sliding, feet possibly still walking. Moonwalk deletes the heel-lift.

Infinite Loop may sew a glide but is a join, not a gait.

Double DollyInterior state made external: the person is carried by an idea.

BoomerangTurn a gesture into a toy.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

In film

Moonwalker and Jackson's music videos are the grammar: the still is the middle of the glide, not a pose at rest. Later videos quote the slide.

Spike Lee's double-dolly is the camera-platform cousin, a different physical cause for a similar dream of locomotion.

Prompt it

Write the slide, not a reverse clip. Still: mid-glide, one foot flat, torso upright, coat trailing.

Video: [Subject] glides backward as if the floor were ice, a moonwalk path. Heel does not lift like a walk.

No spin, no float off the ground, no world rewind.

Use in Video Generator

[Subject] glides backward as if the floor were ice, a moonwalk path.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is walking backward normally, or Reverse Motion. The tell is a heel lift, swinging arms of a walk, or rain rising.

Fix: flat glide, upright torso, floor contact, world still running forward.

Questions

What is Moonwalk in film?

A moonwalk is a backward slide performed as dance grammar: the body glides, the heel does not walk, the world keeps its forward clock.

Moonwalk vs Double Dolly

Double dolly moves performer and camera together so the world slides. Moonwalk is the feet lying: a glide that can be shot with a locked or laterally tracking camera.

When should I use Moonwalk?

When gait is the spectacle and the floor should feel like ice. Skip it on terrain that cannot sell a slide.

How do I prompt Moonwalk for AI image or video?

Write a backward glide, upright torso, one foot sliding, heel not lifting. Keep the world running forward. Ban reverse footage and levitation.
